abstract: This paper investigates the effects of two greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation practices—minimum tillage and mid‐season drainage—on rice farmers' farm performance (e.g., crop yield and risk) and economic outcomes (e.g., income and vulnerability). Minimum tillage reduces carbon dioxide emissions by preserving soil carbon and lowering machinery energy use, while mid‐season drainage reduces methane emissions by interrupting anaerobic conditions in rice paddies. We employ a multinomial endogenous switching regression model to analyse survey data collected from rice farmers in China. The results show that adopting mid‐season drainage alone significantly increases rice yield, while adopting minimum tillage—alone or combined with mid‐season drainage—reduces yield variance. In addition, adoption of either practice or both, substantially improves yield skewness, raises household income and reduces vulnerability to poverty. The findings highlight that promoting GHG mitigation practices like minimum tillage and mid‐season drainage requires emphasising their benefits in reducing production risks and poverty vulnerability, alongside their environmental impact, to encourage broader adoption among farmers.
abstract_zh: 本文探讨了两种温室气体减排措施——少耕与中期排水——对稻农农场绩效（如作物产量与风险）及经济成果（如收入与脆弱性）的影响。少耕通过保持土壤碳含量和降低机械能耗来减少二氧化碳排放，而中期排水则通过中断稻田厌氧条件来减少甲烷排放。我们采用多元内生转换回归模型，分析了来自中国稻农的调查数据。结果显示，单独采用中期排水显著提高了水稻产量，而单独或结合中期排水采用少耕则降低了产量波动性。此外，采用任一措施或两者并用，均显著改善了产量偏度，提高了家庭收入，并降低了贫困脆弱性。研究结果强调，推广如少耕和中期排水等温室气体减排措施时，需着重强调其在降低生产风险与贫困脆弱性方面的益处，以及其环境影响，以促进农民更广泛的采纳。
